provider: Kaggle Notebook outputs (/kaggle/working) — the free side-channel

free_tier.stated: Up to 20 GBs of output from a Notebook may be saved to disk in /kaggle/working. This data is saved automatically and you can then reuse that data in any future Notebook
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: Up to 20 GBs of output from a Notebook may be saved to disk in /kaggle/working. This data is saved automatically and you can then reuse that data in any future Notebook

retention.stated: A Notebook version is a snapshot of your work including your compiled code, log files, output files, data sources, and more.
retention.notes: Additional scratchpad disk space (outside /kaggle/working) that will not be saved outside of the current session

egress.terms: Free download of notebook output files from the version's Output tab, same GCS-backed delivery.

interface_detail: This is a command-line interface tool for interacting via commands in a terminal or shell script
tooling: kaggle CLI (`kaggle kernels output <owner>/<kernel> -p ./dir`) and kagglehub. The notebook executes on managed GPU and TPU compute, writing files directly on the host without local upload transfer.
chaining: By chaining Notebooks as data sources in this way, it’s possible to build pipelines and generate more and better content than you could in a single notebook alone.
limits_note: 20 GB per version is hard; 9 h / 12 h session limits per run; output is only persisted on commit ('Save & Run All'), not on interactive save; GPU/TPU hours are rationed (~30 h/week) but CPU-only runs are not the constraint for pure storage.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Outputs persist indefinitely and are downloadable years later; the flaky part is the commit step (a timed-out run loses the output).
confidence_note: The Kaggle notebooks documentation was read on 2026-11-09 and states the auto-saved output allowance.

extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-09
extras.quota_verbatim: Up to 20 GB of output per notebook version saved to /kaggle/working, and every 'Save & Run All' creates a new version. Outputs are themselves addable as dataset inputs to any future notebook. No documented cap on the number of notebook versions or notebooks per account.
extras.limits_verbatim: 20 GB per version is hard; 9 h / 12 h session limits per run; output is only persisted on commit ('Save & Run All'), not on interactive save; GPU/TPU hours are rationed (~30 h/week) but CPU-only runs are not the constraint for pure storage.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free download of notebook output files from the version's Output tab, same GCS-backed delivery.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 20 GB per notebook version. Notebook versions, notebooks and accounts each carry no stated limit. The reachable total therefore scales with versions and notebooks per account, and a second account carries a second allowance. The whole write path is server-side (the data is produced or fetched inside the notebook, so there is no client uplink bottleneck). This is the standard community alternative route around the 200 GB private quota: a Kaggle forum answer describes it as 'create a new notebook from your dataset and copy files to /kaggle/working'.
extras.tooling_verbatim: kaggle CLI (`kaggle kernels output <owner>/<kernel> -p ./dir`) and kagglehub; the notebook itself runs on free P100/TPU compute so the write happens server-side with no upload from the client at all.
extras.agent_focus: ML/model/data platforms that are not Hugging Face and not ModelScope — the second tier of model and dataset hubs, judged as free bulk storage
